$sources: EN 1991-1-3:2003 Sec 5.2(3)a Eq 5.1, Sec 5.2(7) Table 5.1 (Ce), 5.2(8) (Ct), Sec 5.3.2 Table 5.2 (μ1), Sec 4.3 (Cesl), recommended values

windswept.description: Windswept: flat unobstructed areas exposed on all sides, little or no shelter

normal.description: Normal: no significant removal of snow by wind (terrain, buildings or trees)

sheltered.description: Sheltered: the structure is considerably lower than the surrounding terrain or surrounded by high trees or higher buildings

sources.thermal: EN 1991-1-3 Sec 5.2(8): Ct = 1.0 (less only for roofs of high thermal transmittance, by the National Annex)
sources.shape: EN 1991-1-3 Table 5.2: μ1 = 0.8 for 0° ≤ α ≤ 30°, 0.8 (60 - α)/30 for 30° < α < 60°, 0 for α ≥ 60° (monopitch and duopitch roofs, the undrifted case; drift, μ2 and local effects are not covered)
sources.loadCase: SAEngine practice: the roof snow goes into the roof case Lr, the larger of it and the category H imposed load (EN 1991-1-1 Sec 3.3.2(1): roof imposed loads need not act with snow)
sources.exceptionalFactor: EN 1991-1-3 Sec 4.3, Eq 4.1: Cesl = 2.0 (exceptional snow loads, accidental; reported, not applied)
